newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise on active investment buying.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise on active investment buying.

text.p: Russian MinFin bond prices rose on Monday following Vnesh debt and amid active investment buying after news on Friday of Russian debt rescheduling and payment of the next International Monetary Fund tranche, dealers said.

Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Friday Russia's bank creditors had agreed in principle to reschedule debts of over $20 billion, the critical mass needed for a global rescheduling of $35 billion of debt to go ahead.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Friday also handed over about $350 million to Russia, saying the country's economic reform programme remains on track.

"Everybody is optimistic after this news... Trading started at levels higher than late on Friday because New York operators then pushed them up along with the Vnesh debt," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.
Dealers said foreign investors were mainly behind the rise, with Russian operators ready for speculative selling.
"Russian banks are expecting profit-taking to start at any moment, but demand from the West is still high," one dealer said, adding the market was becoming less liquid.
Dealers said prices were likely to rise more later when U.S. operators joined trading but said it was difficult to forecast the remaining potential of investment buying.
